issues.description: The method messageOnMilk for the Milkable interface is described inconsistently: the UML and code artifacts declare a parameterless method messageOnMilk(), while the Part 2 textual description in the problem statement requires messageOnMilk(double milkVolume). Specifically, problem_statement.md defines the Milkable interface method as messageOnMilk():String (lines 51-53) but later (lines 92-95) instructs students to implement messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and return a string containing the volume. The template and solution code use a no-argument signature: solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java defines messageOnMilk() (line 5), solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java implements public String messageOnMilk() (line 15), and solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java implements public String messageOnMilk() (line 19). The template Main.java calls messageOnMilk() with no arguments in its example/test code (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java, lines 30-32). This contradiction (text vs. UML/code) will confuse students about which signature to implement and may lead to compilation or test failures if tests expect the other signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across problem statement, UML, template, solution, and tests. Two options: (A) Preferred: update the problem statement Part 2 text to require a parameterless messageOnMilk() and change the example return format to "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" so it matches the UML and existing code; update the explanatory sentence at lines 92-95 accordingly. Or (B) if the intent is to track milk volume, change the interface and all implementations to messageOnMilk(double milkVolume), update all call sites (e.g., Main.java and tests) to pass a double, and update the UML and problem statement to match. Prefer option A to align with the provided template and solution; if choosing B, update solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java, Goat.java, Seal.java, the template examples, and any tests to use the double parameter and the volume-containing return format.
